conviction_note: The China upside (Q3 China GMV +25-30% at high-single-digit SSSG, against a full-year China SSSG guide of low single digits) is company-disclosed since 2026-10-09 and was bought +5.8% that day. Against it sit a disputed EPS bar ($0.32 vs $0.37-0.38), overseas weakness guided to low single digits, an October deceleration to low-single-digit SSSG and the last print's -11% on a margin cut. The findings sum to 0.0 and p_up is a slight 55 lean on the arithmetic that the FY revenue guide must rise. abs_move is 7% from confirmed prints, because the baseline's own history is monthly 6-Ks and not prints.

Because the EPS bar is disputed, the findings that depend on it are capped small.

A headline revenue beat alone was already paid for on Oct 9.

next_guide.street_full_year: not found (Capital Securities HK 2026E net profit RMB2.1bn, https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5323354)
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY26 revenue +mid-double-digit; FY adj op margin -3-4pp; H2 China revenue +mid-double-digit; H2 overseas +LSD; net overseas stores -50 to -70 in H2 (https://quartr.com/events/miniso-group-holding-limited-mnso-q2-2026_FLjewQSY)
next_guide.basis: FY25 revenue was RMB21.44bn and H1'26 was RMB11.50bn, so a ~15% FY guide implies H2 of about RMB13.2bn (+9%). If Q3 prints at about +16-18% on the Oct 9 China GMV, the implied Q4 is only about +1-3% against a Q4'25 base of about RMB6.25bn and a street Q4 of $1.07B. Either the FY revenue guide rises or Q4 is guided far below the street. The National Day low-single-digit SSSG argues for a modest raise, not a large one.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-09 MINISO disclosed Q3 Chinese-mainland GMV +25-30% YoY, driven by high-single-digit SSSG and faster than H1 (H1 China revenue +26.2%, Q2 +22.9%). That compares with a full-year China SSSG guide of low single digits (Capital Securities note) and an H2 China revenue guide of mid-double-digit. MINISO USA GMV was about +20% in Q3 and over +30% in September with positive SSSG. China is the profit engine: overseas was only 10-15% of profit in H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose about +5.8% on the day of this update (Simply Wall St 2026-10-10, https://www.webull.com/news/15724655556912128). At the Aug 28 print, revenue was in line and the stock still fell about 11% on margin, so revenue strength has not been paid for at prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: +5.8% on the day and consensus Q3 revenue (~+18%) sits above the guided H2 HSD. What may not be priced is the operating leverage of HSD China SSSG on the China margin. If it had been priced, the EPS consensus would have been revised up after Oct 9; AAII shows 1 down and 0 up in the last month.
findings.independence: Capital Securities HK note restating the update against the FY low-single-digit China SSSG guide (https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5323354). Same underlying company document.

findings.finding: Guide arithmetic: FY26 revenue guided +mid-double-digit on FY25 RMB21.44bn implies H2 of about RMB13.2bn (+9%). Q3 at the Oct 9 run-rate (about RMB6.7-6.85bn, +16-18%) would leave Q4 at only +1-3% against a Q4'25 of about RMB6.25bn and a street Q4 of $1.07B (about RMB7.26bn). The FY revenue guide is therefore likely raised, or else Q4 is guided far below the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last guide change (Aug 28, a margin guide cut): HK shares -11%. Nov 2025: Q4 guided to +25-30% revenue and Deutsche Bank resumed Buy (https://www.itiger.com/news/2586286816).
findings.why_not_priced: Street Q4 at $1.07B already sits above what the unchanged FY guide implies. A raise that only meets the street is partly priced. If a raise were fully expected, sell-side EPS revisions would be rising, not falling.
findings.independence: FY25 revenue of RMB21.44bn from cbndata (https://www.cbndata.com/information/295167). H1 revenue from the company release (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/global/miniso-group-announces-2026-june-quarter-and-interim-unaudited-financial-results-545636.shtml).

findings.finding: The same Oct 9 update said National Day (Oct 1-7) China GMV rose only +20-25% at low-single-digit SSSG, down from high-single-digit SSSG in Q3. The Q4'25 base is demanding: October 2025 China SSSG was in the low teens and Q4'25 revenue was guided +25-30%. Q4 commentary is therefore likely to show a deceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 28 forward-guide cut cost about -11% (HK). The Q4 2025 guide of +25-30% preceded a Buy resumption.
findings.why_not_priced: The company's caveat that holiday data is a short-term snapshot let the market buy the Q3 headline. Street Q4 revenue of $1.07B (about +16%) does not reflect low-single-digit SSSG against a low-teens base.
findings.independence: Q4'25 base from the Nov 2025 Dow Jones note (https://www.itiger.com/news/2586286816) and the Q3'25 release summary (https://marketchameleon.com/Blog/post/2025/11/21/miniso-breaks-through-8000-stores-record-revenue-global-expansion-powers-september-quarter). Shares a document with finding 1. This is the forward half of that update; finding 1 is the quarter half.

findings.finding: The setup is depressed. The stock is -47.6% from its 52-week high and $11.195 sits at the $11 targets of Citi (Neutral) and HSBC (Hold, downgraded) from 2026-08-31. Capital Securities puts it at 9x 2026E earnings with a 6%+ dividend yield, and H1 returns were 121% of adjusted net profit. Against that, it has run +9.2% in 20 days and about +12 points against SPY since Aug 28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have not been rewarded in 2026: Q1 revenue +28.5% was a beat and the stock fell to new lows by June; Q2 fell about 11%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is low on valuation, but the 20-day run-up of +9% shows part of the relief is already in. A fully priced recovery would put spot near the $18 average target, not at the $11 Hold targets.
findings.independence: Analyst actions on Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MNSO/analyst-ratings). Valuation from the Capital Securities note (https://m.gelonghui.com/news/5323354).

findings.finding: The EPS bar is split. Earnings Whispers has $0.37 and Benzinga $0.38, while AAII shows $0.32 from 2 analysts with 1 downward revision in the last month. The company's FY guide (adj net profit down high single digits, adj op margin -3-4pp, H1 adj NP -1.7%) implies H2 adj NP down about 13%. That puts Q3 adj NP at about RMB0.65-0.70bn, or roughly $0.31-0.34 per ADS, below the higher prints of consensus. A 'miss' headline is therefore plausible even on guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2: EPS $0.26 vs $0.30 was a miss and the stock fell about -11% (with the guide cut). The prior quarter missed by 11.8% (AAII).
findings.why_not_priced: Stale aggregator consensus at $0.37-0.38 has not absorbed the August margin cut. If it had, the aggregators would agree at about $0.32. The bar is disputed, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: FY adj net profit HSD decline guide (https://wallstreetcn.com/articles/3780596). Q3'25 adj NP of RMB767m (https://marketchameleon.com/Blog/post/2025/11/21/miniso-breaks-through-8000-stores-record-revenue-global-expansion-powers-september-quarter).

findings.finding: Overseas is in restructuring. The H2 overseas revenue guide is low-single-digit growth with distributor ('agency') revenue down double digits. The H2 plan nets 50-70 fewer overseas stores (100-110 distributor closures, 40-50 new direct stores). Inventory days rose from 214 to 273 in H1 and are to be cleared through promotions. The Oct 9 update said overseas was only 'largely in line' with guidance. Clearance and closure costs fall in Q3 overseas margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Overseas under-delivery was the core of the Aug 28 -11% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Guided and therefore mostly priced. The open question is the margin cost of inventory clearance, which is not quantified anywhere. Net of the rest: China, which is 85-90% of profit, is running above guide (finding 1).
findings.independence: Store and closure plan also in the iTiger/Deep News piece (https://www.itiger.com/news/1125928388). Shares the Aug 28 call with finding 2.

findings.finding: Pop Mart, China's largest designer-toy peer, disclosed on 2026-10-27 Q3 revenue down 45-50% YoY (China -25-30%, Americas -70-75%). That points to a downturn in the IP-toy category in which TOP TOY competes. TOP TOY was RMB575m, about 10% of group revenue, in Q3'25, which grew +111% YoY and is now a hard comparison. TOP TOY slowed to +16.9% in Q2'26.
findings.link: Same product category (designer/IP collectible toys) and the same Chinese mall channel. TOP TOY was about 10% of MINISO group revenue in 25Q3. MINISO's own IP products (YOYO, GMV over RMB1bn in 9M26) sit in the adjacent IP category.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of MNSO reacting to TOP TOY surprises found. MNSO did not fall after Pop Mart's update (baseline: +3.65% on 2026-10-30).
findings.why_not_priced: MNSO rose after Pop Mart's update, so the market is not reading through. If it were, MNSO would have traded down with Pop Mart in late October.
findings.independence: Q2'26 TOP TOY +16.9% from the company release (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/global/miniso-group-announces-2026-june-quarter-and-interim-unaudited-financial-results-545636.shtml).

findings.finding: Yonghui (29.4% equity-accounted by MINISO) reported a Q3'26 attributable net loss of RMB82.7m, including a RMB76m fair-value loss on Advantage Solutions, on revenue down 8.3%. That implies a share of loss to MINISO of roughly RMB24m, if recognised without a lag. This is small, and far below the large Yonghui drag of 2025 (Q2'25 share of loss RMB136.9m), so GAAP net profit improves YoY below operating income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025 Yonghui losses drove the 'net profit halved' headlines (https://www.itiger.com/news/1199486365) but the stock trades on adjusted figures.
findings.why_not_priced: It is below operating income and excluded from adjusted net profit, so it reaches the stock only through GAAP headlines. Sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: Q2'26 Yonghui share of loss of RMB17.2m in the company release (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/global/miniso-group-announces-2026-june-quarter-and-interim-unaudited-financial-results-545636.shtml).

findings.finding: MINISO is buying back stock under a HK$2.0bn 2026 buyback with an automatic repurchase plan. H1 shareholder returns were RMB1.31bn (121% of adjusted net profit) against a 50% payout policy, and the CFO committed to 'stable shareholder returns'. An interim dividend or an extended buyback is likely to be restated with the results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks did not stop the 2026 drawdown (-52% YTD by Sep 1).
findings.why_not_priced: Known and ongoing, so a new authorisation for 2027 would be the incremental part. Mostly priced.

findings.finding: China retail sales grew only +0.4% YoY in August and +1.1% in September 2026, so MINISO's +25-30% China GMV is share gain against a near-flat macro. October retail sales were not yet published at the time of search.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CEO blamed a 'tough domestic consumer market' for the H1 margin miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro, already superseded by the company's own GMV number. This is a proxy and sized near zero.
findings.independence: TrendForce monthly series, quoted via search (https://datatrack.trendforce.com/Chart/content/437/china-total-retail-sales-of-consumer-goods-current-month-yoy).

findings.why_not_priced: This is neutral context, not a mispricing.
